Text 1: Long ago, in the vicinity of Fifth Avenue, there lived a man of great refinement known as the Minamoto Middle Counselor. His wife was the daughter of the Lord Minister. They had one daughter whose name was Lady Kazashi. She was a sight to behold with her lovely cascade of hair, beautiful brow, and shapely lips. In the spring, she spent her waking hours beneath the blossoming branches, and in the autumn, she spent her nights beneath the moon. She was forever composing poems and reciting verses on all sorts of flowers and grasses.

Above all she adored the chrysanthemum. And during the ninth month, the “month of long nights,” she found it nearly impossible to part from her garden. Indeed, this is how she spent the passing years.

Text 2:

After overcoming these barriers, the man visited the young woman nightly without fail. They grew familiar, and the vows he pledged were far from shallow. The woman too returned his affection. The man saw to the needs of the household sending a variety of things at appropriate occasions so that before long, this once impoverished house prospered.

            The nun thought ruefully, “Even I am unsure where this will lead, this affair of the heart.” And yet, because her daughter’s feelings seemed anything but trivial, and because the man was so steadfast in his attentions, she gave her tacit approval, and time went on. The attendants of the household were overjoyed, believing their prayers had been answered and they seemed to be without a care in the world. The nun was dismayed that she had not yet met the man face to face, but with her old-fashioned ways, she felt it was not her place to intrude. As their fortunes changed dramatically, and life became lively and amusing, she was filled with gratitude for the karmic bond that had manifested this mysterious event and her heart was at ease.

Text 3: When it became time to untangle their layered robes, he faced the young lady and tearfully pledged, “I will return another night": 


Enduring the pain of parting
beneath the grasses of remembrance,
the morning dew
forming and then leaving
sorrowful indeed.

(uki koto o   
shinobu ga moto no
asatsuyu no   
okiwakarenan
koto zo kanashiki)

To which the young lady promptly replied:

“Until the end of time”––
to promise such love 
seems fleeting indeed, 
when I hear of the dew on chrysanthemums
beneath the grasses of remembrance. 

(sue made to
chigiri oku koso
hakanakere   
shinobu ga moto no
tsuyu to kiku yori)

<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><path xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" d="M50623.65605,164.84408h693.29057v0h693.29057v709.08427v709.08427h-693.29057h-693.29057v-709.08427z" data-paper-data="{"strokeWidth":2.5,"rotation":0,"annotation":null,"nonHoverStrokeColor":["Color",0,0.81176,1],"editable":true}" id="rectangle_b21fd43e-ced8-4ba7-b8fa-cf97fe0f9025" fill-opacity="0.00001" fill="#00bfff" fill-rule="nonzero" stroke="#00cfff" stroke-width="31.5874" stroke-linecap="butt" stroke-linejoin="miter" stroke-miterlimit="10" stroke-dasharray="" stroke-dashoffset="0" font-family="none" font-weight="none" font-size="none" text-anchor="none" style="mix-blend-mode: normal"/></svg>
Text 4: Having exchanged verses, the mysterious visitor left. He seemed to approach the chrysanthemums at the brushwood fence, whereupon he vanished without a trace.

<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><path xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" d="M48316.9367,133.25667h409.00395v0h409.00395v487.97245v487.97245h-409.00395h-409.00395v-487.97245z" data-paper-data="{"strokeWidth":1,"rotation":0,"deleteIcon":null,"rotationIcon":null,"group":null,"editable":true,"annotation":null}" id="rectangle_35690898-6f9e-4a8d-9064-70fbaa9bba6d" fill-opacity="0" fill="#00bfff" fill-rule="nonzero" stroke="#00bfff" stroke-width="1" stroke-linecap="butt" stroke-linejoin="miter" stroke-miterlimit="10" stroke-dasharray="" stroke-dashoffset="0" font-family="none" font-weight="none" font-size="none" text-anchor="none" style="mix-blend-mode: normal"/></svg>

Text 5: The young lady felt increasingly unsettled, but there was no one reliable in whom she could confide. Despite her best efforts to overcome it, their bond formed on that first encounter proved far from shallow, and they continued to meet in secret. Night after night they spent, until one day, the young lady ventured, “What is it that you conceal from me even now? Come, let me know your name.” Seemingly flustered, the man replied, “In these parts I am known as the Lesser Captain. In time you will come to understand.” Then he departed.

<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><path xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" d="M44723.67255,159.57951h756.46537v0h756.46537v732.77482v732.77482h-756.46537h-756.46537v-732.77482z" data-paper-data="{"strokeWidth":1,"rotation":0,"deleteIcon":null,"rotationIcon":null,"group":null,"editable":true,"annotation":null}" id="rectangle_415296b9-ed1f-4191-bdb3-9f85a04ae14a" fill-opacity="0" fill="#00bfff" fill-rule="nonzero" stroke="#00bfff" stroke-width="1" stroke-linecap="butt" stroke-linejoin="miter" stroke-miterlimit="10" stroke-dasharray="" stroke-dashoffset="0" font-family="none" font-weight="none" font-size="none" text-anchor="none" style="mix-blend-mode: normal"/></svg>

Text 6: Around that time, it was announced that there would be a flower display at the palace. Various courtiers were summoned, and the young lady’s father, the Middle Counselor, attended as well. Calling the Middle Counselor before him, the emperor said, “Bring me chrysanthemum flowers the likes of which are rarely seen in this world.” The Middle Counselor, powerless to refuse an imperial command, replied that he would bring the chrysanthemums and returned home.

<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><path xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" d="M42062.17058,143.78581h487.97245v0h487.97245v740.67167v740.67167h-487.97245h-487.97245v-740.67167z" data-paper-data="{"strokeWidth":1,"rotation":0,"deleteIcon":null,"rotationIcon":null,"group":null,"editable":true,"annotation":null}" id="rectangle_aa681098-b5ad-4059-b635-c812ffa73491" fill-opacity="0" fill="#00bfff" fill-rule="nonzero" stroke="#00bfff" stroke-width="1" stroke-linecap="butt" stroke-linejoin="miter" stroke-miterlimit="10" stroke-dasharray="" stroke-dashoffset="0" font-family="none" font-weight="none" font-size="none" text-anchor="none" style="mix-blend-mode: normal"/></svg>

Text 7: Toward the evening of the same day, the Lesser Captain, looking unusually withered, came to the west wing of the young lady’s residence. He spoke on and on about the ephemeral things of this world and then burst into tears. Because he appeared so inexplicably anguished, the young lady was moved to ask, “What is tormenting you so? Open your heart and tell me everything.” She implored him throughout the night, until he responded, “Why bother keeping anything from you now? Even my visits will end today. How sad to realize that what I thought should have endured for many lives to come has turned to naught!” Silently he wept. “How can this be?” exclaimed the young lady. “I have relied upon you so completely, what will become of me now? How can you say such things? You must take me with you, whether to the end of the fields or deep into the mountains!” There was an unrestrained sadness in her voice. “It is not as I would have wanted . . .” said the Lesser Captain, who had run out of words.

<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><path xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" d="M37649.80507,175.37321h1003.90002v0h1003.90002v719.6134v719.6134h-1003.90002h-1003.90002v-719.6134z" data-paper-data="{"strokeWidth":1,"rotation":0,"deleteIcon":null,"rotationIcon":null,"group":null,"editable":true,"annotation":null}" id="rectangle_05abc752-d6c1-47d2-9797-d0e0666abc57" fill-opacity="0" fill="#00bfff" fill-rule="nonzero" stroke="#00bfff" stroke-width="1" stroke-linecap="butt" stroke-linejoin="miter" stroke-miterlimit="10" stroke-dasharray="" stroke-dashoffset="0" font-family="none" font-weight="none" font-size="none" text-anchor="none" style="mix-blend-mode: normal"/></svg>

Text 8: A while later, the Lesser Captain choked back his tears and said, “I shall swiftly take my leave. Do not forget. Do not forget. As for me, how could I ever let the memory of your affections disappear?” Having said this, he cut off a sidelock, pressed it into a delicate paper embellished with background designs, and wrapped it up. “Whenever you think of me, look upon this,” he said, presenting it to the young lady. “And in the womb, I have left behind a seedling that you should raise ever so carefully. May the child remind you of me.”

<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><path xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" d="M34962.90166,196.43148h1367.15515v0h1367.15515v706.45199v706.45199h-1367.15515h-1367.15515v-706.45199z" data-paper-data="{"strokeWidth":2.5,"rotation":0,"deleteIcon":null,"rotationIcon":null,"group":null,"editable":true,"annotation":null}" id="rectangle_3b858678-52ec-4b45-acdf-7eab4e13c6ef" fill-opacity="0" fill="#00bfff" fill-rule="nonzero" stroke="#00bfff" stroke-width="1" stroke-linecap="butt" stroke-linejoin="miter" stroke-miterlimit="10" stroke-dasharray="" stroke-dashoffset="0" font-family="none" font-weight="none" font-size="none" text-anchor="none" style="mix-blend-mode: normal"/></svg>
Text 9: And so night turned into dawn. The Middle Counselor presented the chrysanthemums to the emperor, who could not take his eyes off them.

<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><path xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" d="M33541.92934,154.31494h509.03072v0h509.03072v490.60474v490.60474h-509.03072h-509.03072v-490.60474z" data-paper-data="{"strokeWidth":2.5,"rotation":0,"deleteIcon":null,"rotationIcon":null,"group":null,"editable":true,"annotation":null}" id="rectangle_a9cac814-d35e-4081-8faf-62a75b0480a6" fill-opacity="0" fill="#00bfff" fill-rule="nonzero" stroke="#00bfff" stroke-width="1" stroke-linecap="butt" stroke-linejoin="miter" stroke-miterlimit="10" stroke-dasharray="" stroke-dashoffset="0" font-family="none" font-weight="none" font-size="none" text-anchor="none" style="mix-blend-mode: normal"/></svg>

Text 10: The young lady waited until evening, but the Lesser Captain never reappeared, not even in her dreams. Oh, how woeful! Although the moon shone through the treetops against the clear midnight sky, tears clouded her heart. She spent night after long sleepless night, until one day she took out the keepsake the man had instructed her to use as a memento. Overwhelmed with emotion, she opened it and discovered a single poem: 


The fragrance  
on your sleeves
I left behind––
how it withers in vain,
the chrysanthemum flower!

 

(nioi o ba
kimi ga tamoto ni 
nokoshiokite
ada ni utsurou
kiku no hana kana)

What she had taken to be a lock of his black hair had all along been a wilted chrysanthemum flower. She felt more unsettled than ever, and thought to herself, “Then even the leaves of verse left behind were composed by none other than the spirit of the chrysanthemum.”

<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><path xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" d="M30543.01807,159.57951h832.8016v0h832.8016v740.67167v740.67167h-832.8016h-832.8016v-740.67167z" data-paper-data="{"strokeWidth":2.5,"rotation":0,"deleteIcon":null,"rotationIcon":null,"group":null,"editable":true,"annotation":null}" id="rectangle_6b71453d-df2b-414e-b7c4-b9530b829955" fill-opacity="0" fill="#00bfff" fill-rule="nonzero" stroke="#00bfff" stroke-width="1" stroke-linecap="butt" stroke-linejoin="miter" stroke-miterlimit="10" stroke-dasharray="" stroke-dashoffset="0" font-family="none" font-weight="none" font-size="none" text-anchor="none" style="mix-blend-mode: normal"/></svg>

Text 11: Making her way into a garden of white chrysanthemums, she cried, “The poet wrote that ‘the blossoms may scatter, but the roots will never die,’  and thus your fate is known. Even if you are a chrysanthemum spirit, I beseech you to exchange with me your leaves of verse just once more.” She appeared at her wits end, and the reason was all too clear. “If there had been no flower-gathering at the palace, then I would have no such despair. Whatever the case may be, I am not long for this world.” To even contemplate such thoughts was excruciating. 

“Hurry, hurry, come to me Lesser Captain! In whose care will you leave me? Oh, where could you be? The sadness of our mortal lives! Although you said again and again that this was the end, I assumed you were just talking about the ordinary fleetingness of the world. How can this be? Oh, how wretched! Am I dreaming or awake?” She went on and on, bewildered, sinking to the ground in despair. He had left her only with instructions never to forget. Now it was clear that those had indeed been his final parting words. Distraught, she continued, “Alas, I will give my life for that fragile vow! Let us see each other once more!” She was in a certain maternal condition and grieved ceaselessly the entire time. How sad her nurse must have been to see the young lady so distressed.

<svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg'><path xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" d="M26978.45693,177.49823h1336.90308v0h1336.90308v733.1506v733.1506h-1336.90308h-1336.90308v-733.1506z" data-paper-data="{"strokeWidth":1,"rotation":0,"deleteIcon":null,"rotationIcon":null,"group":null,"editable":true,"annotation":null}" id="rectangle_191726a0-2f06-4072-9fb4-665d1f075409" fill-opacity="0" fill="#00bfff" fill-rule="nonzero" stroke="#00bfff" stroke-width="1" stroke-linecap="butt" stroke-linejoin="miter" stroke-miterlimit="10" stroke-dasharray="" stroke-dashoffset="0" font-family="none" font-weight="none" font-size="none" text-anchor="none" style="mix-blend-mode: normal"/></svg>
Text 12: After the nurse told the young lady’s mother the state of things, she and the Middle Counselor were beside themselves. They tried to help in whatever way they could, but to no avail.

Text 13: The nurse sought the help of a spirit medium, saying, “My young lady, just fifteen years of age, has been ill ever since the evening of the last day of the ninth month. Just what should we do? Please perform a divination.”

Text 14: The spirit master spoke: “The divination you ask for is difficult to read. Could she perhaps be in a certain condition? However viewed, the signs suggest peril.”  The nurse rushed back home with an eerie feeling and relayed all of this to the young lady’s mother. The lady responded, “I too suspected that she might be in that way, but naturally I hesitated to speak up, assuming that you would know of such a thing. What if they meet again? Go question her thoroughly.” 

Heeding her words, the nurse headed for the adjacent quarters and went straight to the young lady’s side. “By the looks of you,” she said, “you do not seem at all like your usual self. There must be something you are concealing from me.” Continuing in a delicate whisper, she said, “Please, open up your heart.” The young lady knew it should remain a secret, but she longed to talk about it. Though deeply embarrassed, she recounted the affair from beginning to end, sparing no detail. The nurse was astonished.

Text 16: The days and months slowly passed and the young lady grew ever weaker and more helpless. Then, with her own nurse and numerous ladies attending to the delivery, she gave birth to a beautiful baby girl. The Middle Counselor and his wife felt boundless affection for the child. And yet the young lady seemed to be nearing the end.

Text 17: he Middle Counselor and his wife were beside themselves with grief. The young lady had her mother and father brought near, and she tearfully addressed them, saying, “Take that truism to heart, that all living things must one day vanish, and do not lament my passing. What matters most is the little girl whom I leave behind in this world. Although I myself will have passed away, please do not forget her. I am overcome with regret that I must precede my mother and father on this journey. How wretched you must think me. It is excruciating indeed to leave behind so many people, but most of all my mother and father.” Uttering these final words, she faded with the morning dew. The Middle Counselor and his wife were at a complete loss. The nurse, immersed in grief, swiftly took the tonsure. Such a profoundly moving thing is difficult to put into words.

Text 19: The years went by and before they knew it, the girl turned thirteen. Her looks were exquisite. “Surely she would surpass the likes of Yang Guifei of Tang, Lady Li of Han, or, in our land, Princess Sotoori and Ono no Komachi!” the people all exclaimed.  Before long word of her beauty had reached the ears of the emperor. By his order she was made a consort. The Middle Counselor and his wife were overjoyed. Rumor had it that the Emperor loved her above all others. His feelings for her grew only deeper and before long a prince and princess were born in quick succession. Everyone remarked how truly fortunate this was.
